Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

positive adjective

favourable, approving: of an answer, a reaction, a result

also favourable, favorable, a positive answer, positive feedback, a positive result

classical

Cic. Tusc. 2.4: secundō populō, with the people’s approval (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Lael. 22: secundās rēs
Traupman 314

secundus, secunda, secundum

adjective, declension

favourable, approving; going well

Properly “following”, as a fair wind or the current follows a boat (see current); rēs secundae are good times, the opposite of rēs adversae.

Other words

  • benignus, benigna, benignum — kind, favourable (of an answer or a hearing)

    adjective, declension · also used · classical · Sall. Jug. 11.1: benignē respondēre (Lewis & Short); Liv. 27.4.7 (Lewis & Short)

    A positive answer is given benignē, kindly.

  • prosperus (prosper), prospera, prosperum — favourable, successful (of an outcome)

    adjective · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 9.7.1: prosperōs exitūs

    See successful.

Examples

  • nam et secundās rēs splendidiōrēs facit amīcitia et adversās partiēns commūnicānsque leviōrēs

    for friendship makes good fortune brighter, and bad fortune lighter by dividing and sharing itCic. Lael. 22

See also positive, successful.
